source.title: Iowa DNR LabCert — List of Certified Labs (Drinking Water)
limitations: Transcribed from Iowa DNR LabCert Lab Listing generated 9/7/2026. Only rows whose Program includes Drinking Water are considered.
In-state Commercial labs with Drinking Water are tabulated (11). Out-of-state Commercial labs with Drinking Water on the same roster are omitted — use LabCert for the full list.
Municipal utility / water works / WWTP / WRF / regional water association labs are omitted even when they hold Drinking Water certification.
Industrial/Private labs (including Iowa Soybean Association Water Lab) are omitted. Nonpotable-only labs and DNR (Test - Not a Lab) are omitted.

State Hygienic Laboratory (Coralville, Lakeside, Ankeny) is treated as verified for private wells based on DNR Private Well Testing guidance plus SHL’s Request Private Well Testing page (coliform bacteria and nitrate kit).

County / district health labs with Drinking Water (Dubuque County, Siouxland District, Linn County) are listed separately; private-well acceptance at each lab address is unknown unless confirmed by calling — DNR says county environmental health can arrange testing / PWG.
LabCert does not state per-lab private-well acceptance for commercial rows. Accepts private wells = unknown — call first. Mail/drop-off = unknown.
PWG grant dollar amounts for well services appear on the DNR well-testing page; this directory intentionally omits analysis prices and does not copy service grant dollars onto the public HTML.
Phone numbers normalized to (XXX) XXX-XXXX when 10 digits were present. Addresses kept as printed on LabCert.

verified_private_well.name: State Hygienic Laboratory at the University of Iowa (Coralville, Lakeside, Ankeny)
verified_private_well.path: Order a private-well kit via SHL Request Private Well Testing; or arrange testing through county environmental health / Private Well Grants
verified_private_well.notes: SHL’s request-private-well-testing page (retrieved 7 September 2026) offers a kit for coliform bacteria and nitrate and notes funding may be available through county health departments and the Private Well Grants Program. Iowa DNR Private Well Testing states county environmental health can help arrange testing and that analysis should be performed by DNR Certified Drinking Water Laboratories; it also points readers to SHL’s private well site.

labs.source_document: Iowa DNR LabCert — List of Certified Labs (Date Generated: 9/7/2026)
labs.notes: State Hygienic Laboratory location on Iowa DNR LabCert with Drinking Water (Date Generated 9/7/2026). Verified for private wells because Iowa DNR Private Well Testing points well owners to SHL and SHL publishes a Request Private Well Testing kit form for coliform bacteria and nitrate. County Private Well Grants may fund testing — contact your county environmental health office. Confirm location, kit instructions, and holding times with SHL before you collect. Prices intentionally omitted.
